title: Cellular Respiration
standard_text: Glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain; ATP yield; aerobic and anaerobic respiration; fermentation and its uses. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 1, Quarter 2)
meta_desc: Free Biology 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 2): respiration, aTP and comparing the processes, glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, electron transport and fermentation and anaerobic respiration. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Anaerobic respiration releases much less energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Respiration releases energy from glucose, which is stored in ATP. Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into pyruvate; in aerobic respiration the pyruvate enters the mitochondria, where the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain produce most of the ATP, carbon dioxide and water.

Without oxygen, cells respire anaerobically. In muscles, pyruvate becomes lactic acid, causing fatigue. In yeast, it becomes ethanol and carbon dioxide (alcoholic fermentation), which is used to make bread and beer.

Example

Where does the Krebs cycle happen?

The powerhouse of the cell

Answer: in the mitochondria

Example

What does yeast make in anaerobic respiration?

Fermentation

Answer: ethanol and carbon dioxide

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration is the same as breathing.
  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Thinking anaerobic respiration makes more energy.

faq.a: Yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide, which forms bubbles in the dough.

faq.q: Why do you breathe hard after a race?
faq.a: To supply oxygen to break down the lactic acid (the oxygen debt).

items.q: A competitive inhibitor slows an enzyme. How does it work?
c: it has a similar shape to the substrate and blocks the active site
items.e: Adding more substrate reduces its effect.

items.q: Where does glycolysis take place?
items.e: Glucose is split into two pyruvate.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 3 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: What happens in the link reaction?
c: pyruvate is oxidized to acetyl CoA, releasing CO₂ and reducing NAD
items.e: It takes place in the matrix.

items.q: An organism takes in 20 cm³ of oxygen and gives out 14 cm³ of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.700 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: Where does the electron transport chain of aerobic respiration take place?
c: on the inner membrane (cristae) of the mitochondrion
items.e: Most ATP is made here.

items.q: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
c: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ ATP)
items.e: It releases energy as ATP.

items.q: What is the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration?
items.e: Oxygen combines with electrons and protons to form water.

items.q: Why is a respirometer kept at constant temperature?
c: temperature changes gas volume and enzyme activity
items.e: Use a water bath and a control tube.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 9 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 18 ATP.

items.q: What is a limiting factor?
c: the factor that is present in excess
the factor that is in shortest supply and so controls the rate
a factor that stops a reaction for ever
the temperature at which an enzyme denatures
items.e: Light, CO₂ and temperature limit photosynthesis.

items.q: What is the respiratory quotient (RQ) of carbohydrates?
items.e: CO₂ given out = O₂ taken in.

items.q: Why does anaerobic respiration make much less ATP?
c: only glycolysis produces ATP; the Krebs cycle and electron transfer chain stop
items.e: Only 2 ATP per glucose.

items.q: What is the role of NAD in respiration?
c: it carries hydrogen (protons and electrons) to the electron transfer chain
items.e: It is reduced in glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 3 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 6 ATP.

items.q: What do the light-dependent reactions supply to the Calvin cycle?
items.e: Water is split and oxygen is released.

items.q: Where is the electron transfer chain?
items.e: Folding into cristae gives a large surface area.

items.q: An organism takes in 50 cm³ of oxygen and gives out 36 cm³ of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.720 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: Why is anaerobic respiration much less efficient than aerobic respiration?
c: it makes no ATP at all
glucose is only partly broken down, so much less ATP is made
items.e: Energy is left in lactate or ethanol.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP from glycolysis of one glucose?
items.e: 4 are made but 2 are used.

items.q: What is the name for the cycle in the stroma that fixes CO₂ into sugar?
items.e: Calvin cycle: the cycle in the stroma that fixes CO₂ into sugar.

items.q: What is photorespiration?
c: the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants
RuBisCO binding O₂ instead of CO₂, wasting energy
a reaction center chlorophyll an absorbing best at 700 nm (P700)
a reaction center chlorophyll an absorbing best at 680 nm (P680)
items.e: Photorespiration: RuBisCO binding O₂ instead of CO₂, wasting energy.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 9 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 9 = 18.

items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 14 ATP.

items.q: Where does the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) take place?
c: in the stroma of the chloroplast
items.e: CO₂ is fixed by the enzyme RuBisCO.

items.q: What is formed when pyruvate enters the mitochondrion?
c: acetyl CoA, with release of CO₂ and NADH
items.e: This is oxidative decarboxylation.

items.q: Where in the cell does fermentation take place?
items.e: Fermentation: the cytoplasm, without oxygen.

items.q: What is the name for RuBisCO binding O₂ instead of CO₂, wasting energy?
items.e: Photorespiration: RuBisCO binding O₂ instead of CO₂, wasting energy.

items.q: Which factor would NOT increase the rate of photosynthesis in a plant already in bright light at 25 °C with low CO₂?
c: a slightly warmer temperature up to the optimum
items.e: When CO₂ is limiting, extra light makes no difference.

items.q: Why does each enzyme work on only one substrate?
c: the active site has a shape that fits only that substrate
enzymes are used up after one reaction
enzymes are too large for other substrates
all substrates have the same shape
items.e: Lock-and-key and induced-fit models.

items.q: Why is respiration called an amphibolic pathway?
c: it is used both for breaking down and for building molecules
it happens in water and on land
items.e: Intermediates are used to make fats and proteins.

items.q: What is the first product of the Krebs cycle?
items.e: Acetyl CoA + oxaloacetic acid → citric acid.

items.q: What is PEP carboxylase?
c: large bundle-sheath cells around the veins of C₄ leaves
the splitting of water that releases oxygen
the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants
the cycle in the stroma that fixes CO₂ into sugar
items.e: PEP carboxylase: the enzyme that fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells of C₄ plants.

items.e: Fats enter as acetyl CoA, proteins as amino acids.

items.e: Protons flow out through ATP synthase.

items.e: Green is reflected.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidize 6 molecules of glucose completely?

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidize 2 molecules of glucose completely?

items.q: What is the RQ of fats such as tripalmitin?
items.e: Fats need more oxygen to burn.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 2 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidize 1 molecule of glucose completely?

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidize 9 molecules of glucose completely?

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 10 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 4 molecules of glucose?

items.q: Which enzyme makes ATP in the inner mitochondrial membrane?
items.e: Protons flow through it.

items.q: What is the end product of glycolysis?
items.e: Glucose → 2 pyruvic acid.
